lines.text: IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE ITBDI
The California Constitution and Education Code authorize a school district to issue bonds
for specified purposes if approved at an election by 55% of those voting on issuance of the
bonds. [291
The Board of Trustees of the Burlingame Elementary School District (District) proposes
this Measure, which would authorize the District to issue bonds in a principal amount not to
exceed $100 million. The bonds will have an interest rate not exceeding the legal maximum and
will be repaid within the time permitted by law. The Tax Rate Statement printed in this pamphlet
contains the District's best estimates of tax rates required to service the bond debt during the life
of the bonds, which is anticipated to last until June 2058. The District's best estimate of the
average annual tax rate levy to fund this bond is $16.00 per $100,000 ($0.016/$100) of assessed
valuation. The District estimates that the total amount repayable during the life of the bond,
including principal and interest, will be approximately $195.5 million. [1251
The California Constitution requires the listing of specific projects to be funded from the
bond revenue and certification that the District Board of Trustees has evaluated safety, class size
reduction, and information technology needs in the development of that list. The Bond Project
List can be found in the full text of the Measure, and includes without limitation: [531
Construct, acquire, renovate, and equip classrooms, science labs, libraries, and other
instructional facilities;
Repair or replace leaky roofs, aging exterior walls, flooring, and ceilings;
Replace aging and inefficient plumbing, electrical, and HVAC systems;
Replace portable classrooms with permanent classrooms;
Upgrade technology, computers, and network infrastructure;
Upgrade security, fire, and safety systems, including security cameras and access
controls;
Complete accessibility improvements required by law;
Repair, replace, or upgrade paved surfaces, parking, and outdoor facilities; and
Make other repairs and improvements to modernize school facilities. [921
The Measure authorizes equipment acquisition, upgrades, repairs, services, construction,
and other items related to the listed projects. The Bond Project List does not imply a specific
prioritization among the projects, and should be reviewed for further details. 1351
No proceeds from the bonds shall be used for teacher or administrator salaries or other
school operating expenses, except to reimburse the District for the cost of staff time spent
working on the bond projects themselves. [361
State law requires that the District take certain steps to account for the proceeds from the
bonds. Accordingly, the District will appoint an independent citizens' oversight committee,
establish a special account for deposit of the bond proceeds, and conduct annual independent
performance and financial audits to ensure that bond funds are spent only for the purposes listed
in the Bond Project List and for no other purposes. [651
A "yes" vote on this Measure would authorize the District to issue bonds in a principal
amount not to exceed $100 million for the purposes listed in the Bond Project List. [281
A "no" vote would prevent the District from issuing the bonds. [Ill
This Measure passes if at least 55% of those voting on the Measure vote "yes." [151
End of Analysis
